label: early original-phase input of z/f (t=1-3), or of a b-e/p-w/3 token at t=2
explanation: Position x token-identity unit for the start of the original phase. 96% of activation mass is in the original phase at t=1..3 (67% at t=2); it never fires at t=0 or at t>=7 of the input. Tokens z and f fire at near-100% precision at t=1, 2 and 3. At t=2 a wider set also fires: b, e, q, u (precision 0.96-1.0), c, t, 3 (0.8-0.9), w, p, s, d (0.55-0.7). Other letters and digits 0-2 almost never fire. Magnitude is highest for z, then f; the top activations are z at t=2, especially right after a z at t=1 (e.g. i z z ...), and lower-quartile activations are mostly the weaker t=2 tokens (w, p, q, b). Small leftovers (about 10% of mass) are weak activations at t=4-5 on z/f, a few other t=2 tokens, and rare copy-phase steps in short sequences when z/f/t are input or output. It is essentially silent at the delimiter and during copying.

issues: The core of the claim holds. On test the predicate scores P 0.873, R 0.764, F1 0.815, mass recall 0.901. The unit never fires at t=0 or at original positions t>=5, about 67% of activation mass is at t=2, and the token precisions at t=2 for z, f, e, q, u, t, 3, c and w/p/s/d match what was reported.

The claim that digits 0-2 'almost never fire' is wrong. At t=2, precision is 0.35 for digit 1, 0.24 for 2 and 0.18 for 0. Letters n (0.26), j (0.20) and o (0.19) are also well above zero. The response at t=2 is a graded token weight, not a clean set of firing tokens.

There is a systematic context effect the label leaves out. For the medium and weak tokens at t=2, firing depends strongly on the first token orig(0). If orig(0) is i, precision is 0.95; for r it is 0.89, for j 0.84, for g 0.79 and for l 0.77. If orig(0) is q, c or u it drops to 0.04-0.15. prev_tok matters too: after z, precision is 0.95. The top examples all begin with i or r, which fits this.

The explanation calls the copy-phase activity 'rare'. In fact the last copy step of every L=3 sequence (t=5) fires 65% of the time (precision 0.645, 2.6% of recall). That rate is near 1.0 when the input there is e, z, f or t, and near 0 when it is r. This is a separate, systematic case of activity, not scattered noise.
Missed activations hold 24% of active steps (9.9% of mass). They are mostly t=2 tokens outside the list whose firing depends on context, other tokens at t=3, and the L=3 final copy step.
skeptic.revised_label: Early original phase: z/f input at t=1-3, or many other tokens at t=2 with token-graded strength that is boosted when the sequence starts with i/r/j/g/l. Also fires at the last copy step of length-3 sequences.
